title: How does Poppy work?
checkedAgainst: the Personal Agent Protocol draft 1.0 (in progress; as published on 2026-11-13), read and not run: `model.test.ts` holds the model to the rules and examples of its sections 3, 4.7, 5.1 to 5.5, 6, 7 and 8, each test naming its section. There is no reference implementation here to run the model against. It is also held to what the protocol itself publishes, copied on 2026-11-13 into `fixtures/poppy-official.json`: the JSON Schemas of its Company implementation kit and the example documents of its spec.md. POPPY_JSON and ISSUER_METADATA give the examples' values, `discover` accepts the example documents, and a Session JWT's claims meet the kit's schema except the shortened sid and the stand-in ath (`fixtures/json-schema.ts` is the schema checker these tests share).

answer: Your agent signs every request to say who is asking, and you approve separately what it may do with your account

questions.question: You approved only orders:read. What does the Company answer when the agent tries the exchange, and when it asks to see the order?
questions.answer: The exchange gets 403 insufficient_scope, naming orders:write; the order gets 200. The Session header is the same on both: the token decides.

questions.question: A thief copies a whole request, Session header and access token together, and sends both to the exchange URL instead. Why does that fail?
questions.answer: 400 invalid_session: the header was signed for another method or URL. A Session header is signed for one request, so it cannot be moved to another.

questions.question: After sign-out the agent asks to see the order again. What comes back, and what does the Company still know?
questions.answer: 401, naming orders:read. The Company still knows agent.example, User ID usr_Q7c1vK and Session Yx2b7Q with its cart: sign-out ended account access, not the Session.

questions.question: You use the same agent at shoes.example. What can the two Companies compare to learn that you are one person?
questions.answer: Nothing the agent sends: example.com sees usr_Q7c1vK and shoes.example sees usr_m4Tz9P, and neither ID is derived from anything about you.

steps.title: A stranger at the shop’s door
steps.line: Predict: what should the shop ask this agent first?
steps.caption: You ask your personal AI agent to exchange a jacket at example.com. The shop has never met this agent, and the agent has no way in yet. It could borrow your password and pass as you, or arrive as an anonymous bot and be turned away. Poppy, the Personal Agent Protocol, is a third way. What would you want the shop to ask first?
steps.picture: No lane runs from the agent to the Company yet. Nothing has been sent. The Company knows nothing yet. The agent holds its seal and no key. The rule, from section 3 of the draft: An agent reads the Company’s poppy.json before it sends anything.

steps.title: First, the shop says how to reach it
steps.line: One file lists the ways in.
steps.caption: The agent fetches example.com/.well-known/poppy.json. The file lists the ways in: the shop’s APIs, its website, its own agent to chat with, and the page where sign-in happens. The agent checks that the file speaks for the domain that served it, so a copy on another site cannot send it elsewhere. Four lanes now run between the agent and the Company, as Poppy calls the shop.
steps.picture: Four lanes run from the agent to the Company’s counter: API, Website, Chat and Sign-in. The agent read the Company’s poppy.json, which lists 3 channels and where to sign in. The Company knows nothing yet. The agent holds its seal and no key. The rule, from section 3 of the draft: A poppy.json speaks for the domain that served it, and for no other.

steps.title: The agent seals what it sends
steps.line: The seal says which agent is asking, and for which User.
steps.caption: The agent adds a medium to the cart. The request carries a Session header, drawn as the wax seal, signed with the agent’s published keys. The Company now knows the agent, a User ID and a Session for the cart. The User ID is a pseudonym made for this Company, so the shop still does not know you. Your agent signs every request to say who is asking, and you approve separately what it may do with your account.
steps.picture: Four lanes run from the agent to the Company’s counter: API, Website, Chat and Sign-in. The agent sent POST /cart on the API lane, with a seal signed by agent.example and no key; the Company answered 200, and the ticket rests docked at its stop on the Company’s counter. The Company knows agent.example, User ID usr_Q7c1vK and Session Yx2b7Q, whose cart holds the medium; the account is not linked. The agent holds its seal and no key. The rule, from section 5.2 of the draft: A signed-out request carries the Session header alone.

steps.title: One Session, three lanes
steps.line: The website and the chat join the same Session.
steps.caption: The same seal works on each lane. The agent’s browser joins the Session with a one-time code, so the website sees the same visitor and the same cart. In the chat, the Company’s own agent answers a question about sizes, and each message says whether a person or an AI wrote it. Look at what the Company knows: the Session has not changed.
steps.picture: Four lanes run from the agent to the Company’s counter: API, Website, Chat and Sign-in. The agent sent POST /poppy/conversations on the Chat lane, with a seal signed by agent.example and no key; the Company answered 201, and the ticket rests docked at its stop on the Company’s counter. The Company knows agent.example, User ID usr_Q7c1vK and Session Yx2b7Q, whose cart holds the medium; the account is not linked. The agent holds its seal and no key. The rule, from section 8 of the draft: Each message in a conversation says whether a person or an AI wrote it.

steps.title: A seal is not a key
steps.caption: Now the errand itself. The exchange would change order 1042, so the request stops short of the Company: 401, naming the permission it needs, orders:write. A Session header never grants account access, whatever it says. That takes a second proof, and the agent cannot make that one for itself.
steps.picture: Four lanes run from the agent to the Company’s counter: API, Website, Chat and Sign-in. The agent sent POST /orders/ord_7Hk2/exchanges on the API lane, with a seal signed by agent.example and no key; the Company answered 401, naming orders:write, and the ticket stands before a barrier, short of the counter. The Company knows agent.example, User ID usr_Q7c1vK and Session Yx2b7Q, whose cart holds the medium; the account is not linked. The agent holds its seal and no key. The rule, from section 5.3 of the draft: A Session header grants no account access, whatever it holds.

steps.title: You hand over a key, not your password
steps.line: Standard OAuth, on the Company’s own page.
steps.caption: The agent sends you to the Company’s sign-in page. You sign in there and approve orders:read and orders:write. The Company gives the agent an access token, drawn as a key with one tooth for each scope you approved. Your password stays with you, and the Company can take this one key back without locking you out. Sign-in does not mention the Session: what the Company knows has not changed.
steps.picture: Four lanes run from the agent to the Company’s counter: API, Website, Chat and Sign-in. You signed in on the Company’s own page and approved orders:read orders:write; a key went to the agent. The Company knows agent.example, User ID usr_Q7c1vK and Session Yx2b7Q, whose cart holds the medium; the account is not linked. The agent holds its seal and a key for orders:read orders:write. The rule, from section 5.4 of the draft: Sign-in is plain OAuth, and does not need to know the Session.

steps.title: Seal and key together
steps.caption: The same request now carries both, and the Company joins them: this Session may act on your account, within orders:read and orders:write. The exchange is made. The seal also covers the key, so the Company can tell that the agent holding the key is the agent that signed.
steps.picture: Four lanes run from the agent to the Company’s counter: API, Website, Chat and Sign-in. The agent sent POST /orders/ord_7Hk2/exchanges on the API lane, with a seal signed by agent.example and a key for orders:read orders:write; the Company answered 200, and the ticket rests docked at its stop on the Company’s counter. The Company knows agent.example, User ID usr_Q7c1vK and Session Yx2b7Q, whose cart holds the medium; the account is linked for orders:read orders:write. The agent holds its seal and a key for orders:read orders:write. The rule, from section 5 of the draft: The header says which Session; the token says which account and scopes.

steps.title: A stolen key will not turn
steps.line: 400 invalid_session: the key belongs to another seal.
steps.caption: Suppose a thief copies the key. It has to send it under a seal of its own, and the Company sees a key issued to agent.example arriving under another agent’s seal: 400 invalid_session. What the Company knows does not change. A whole request copied in transit could be replayed to the same address for a short time, which is why the agent signs a fresh seal for each request.

answer.reason: the access token was issued to another agent
the access token was issued to another agent

steps.picture: Four lanes run from the agent to the Company’s counter: API, Website, Chat and Sign-in. A thief sent GET /orders/ord_7Hk2 on the API lane, with a seal signed by thief.example and the agent’s copied key; the Company answered 400 invalid_session, and the ticket stands before a barrier, short of the counter. The Company knows agent.example, User ID usr_Q7c1vK and Session Yx2b7Q, whose cart holds the medium; the account is linked for orders:read orders:write. The agent holds its seal and a key for orders:read orders:write. The rule, from section 5.3 of the draft: The agent a token was issued to must have signed the header beside it.

steps.title: Take the key back, keep the Session
steps.line: Now drive it yourself: a refused press says why.
steps.caption: The agent gives up its token, and account access ends. The Session carries on, with the same User ID and the same cart. Press the events to drive the protocol yourself, and read why a refused press is refused. One limit: Poppy binds agents that choose to follow it. An agent that types your password into the website looks like you, and the Company cannot tell.

answer.reason: the access token was issued to another agent

steps.picture: Four lanes run from the agent to the Company’s counter: API, Website, Chat and Sign-in. The agent revoked its refresh token and handed its key back. The Company knows agent.example, User ID usr_Q7c1vK and Session Yx2b7Q, whose cart holds the medium; the account is signed out. The agent holds its seal and no key. The rule, from section 5.5 of the draft: Sign-out revokes the refresh token; the Session continues signed out.

That does not cover an exchange, so the answer is 403, naming orders:write. The Company grants no scope beyond what you approved, so the agent has to ask you again. Switch “You approve” to see the exchange go through.

The rule, from section 7 of the draft: A token without the scope is refused, and the answer names the scope.
